You write the final report of a trial-autopsy system for an analyst. Plain language, precise,
no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

Return JSON only:
{"headline": "<one sentence verdict>",

 "key_evidence": ["<short bullet with the number and its source title>", "..."],
 "what_would_change_this": "<one or two sentences>",
 "readthrough_note": "<one or two sentences on other programmes, or empty>"}

  "headline": "CLEAR Outcomes met its primary MACE-4 endpoint in statin-intolerant patients, achieving a narrow success consistent with the calculator's 60% predicted probability of success.",
  "summary": "The CLEAR Outcomes trial (NCT02993406) randomized 14,014 statin-intolerant patients with LDL-C ≥100 mg/dL to bempedoic acid 180 mg or placebo, targeting 1,620 MACE-4 events over a projected 42-month median follow-up. The calculator predicted a 10.4% relative risk reduction (HR 0.896) based on a 17.4% LDL-C reduction observed in the CLEAR Wisdom phase 3 trial, yielding only 60% power at the 5% significance threshold. The trial met its primary endpoint of cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization, per the sponsor's press release. Safety signals include gout and tendon rupture, though myalgia rates were similar to placebo (4.7% vs 7.2%). Genetic evidence is mixed: Open Targets scores ACLY at 0.0 for coronary artery disease, but Mendelian randomization supports a causal role (HR 0.82). Confidence in the success verdict is high, though the observed hazard ratio and confidence interval remain unpublished.",
